ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A cuboid-shaped container that is not filled completely contains $120 \mathrm{~m}^{3}$ of water. The depth of the water is either $2 \mathrm{~m}$ or $3 \mathrm{~m}$ or $5 \mathrm{~m}$, depending on which side the container is actually standing on (drawings not to scale). How big is the volume of the container?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The picture shows the same rectangular cuboid container placed on three different side faces, with the same amount of water; the gray part represents water. The water depths marked under the three placements are respectively 2 m, 3 m, and 5 m. Reasoning: Let the three edge lengths of the rectangular cuboid be a, b, c. The volume of water in the container is fixed at 120 m³. Water depth = volume of water / base area, so the base areas corresponding to the three placements are respectively 120/2 = 60 m², 120/3 = 40 m², and 120/5 = 24 m². These three base areas are some arrangement of ab, ac, bc. Therefore (abc)^2 = (ab)(ac)(bc) = 60 × 40 × 24 = 57600. Since abc is positive, abc = √57600 = 240. The total volume of the rectangular cuboid container is 240 m³.

method.method_draft: Let the cuboid side lengths be a, b, c. From the image/text, the same 120 m^3 of water has depths 2 m, 3 m, and 5 m when the cuboid is placed on its three different pairs of opposite faces. Use depth = water volume / base area. Thus the three possible base areas are 120/2 = 60, 120/3 = 40, and 120/5 = 24 square meters; these are ab, ac, and bc in some order. Then (abc)^2 = (ab)(ac)(bc) = 60·40·24 = 57600, so abc = 240. Therefore the container volume is 240 m^3.

推理：设长方体的三条边长为 a、b、c。容器内水的体积固定为 120 m³。水深 = 水的体积 / 底面积，所以三种摆放对应的底面积分别是 120/2 = 60 m²，120/3 = 40 m²，120/5 = 24 m²。这三个底面积就是 ab、ac、bc 的某种排列。因此 (abc)^2 = (ab)(ac)(bc) = 60 × 40 × 24 = 57600。因为 abc 为正，所以 abc = √57600 = 240。长方体容器的总体积为 240 m³。

method.method_draft: Let r be the fraction of the container volume occupied by water, so r = 120/V where V is the full container volume. In any orientation, the water depth is the same fraction r of the vertical side length, because water volume/full volume = depth/full height for a rectangular prism with the same base. The image/text gives the three water depths as 2, 3, and 5 meters, so the actual three side lengths of the cuboid are 2/r, 3/r, and 5/r. Hence V = (2/r)(3/r)(5/r) = 30/r^3. Since the water volume is rV = 120, we get r·30/r^3 = 120, so 30/r^2 = 120, r = 1/2. Therefore V = 120/r = 240 m^3.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The image shows the same cuboid-shaped container standing on three different sides. In each orientation it is partially filled with water, and the marked water depths are 2 m, 3 m, and 5 m respectively.

Reasoning: Let V be the full volume of the cuboid container, and let r be the fraction of the container occupied by water. Since the water volume is 120 m^3, r = 120/V. For a rectangular prism in any orientation, the ratio water depth/full vertical side length equals the ratio water volume/full container volume, so this ratio is r. Therefore the three side lengths of the cuboid are 2/r, 3/r, and 5/r. Hence V = (2/r)(3/r)(5/r) = 30/r^3. Also, the water volume is rV = 120, so r · 30/r^3 = 120, giving 30/r^2 = 120. Thus r^2 = 1/4, and since r > 0, r = 1/2. Therefore V = 120/r = 120/(1/2) = 240 m^3.
